key_insight: AdsNet predicts adsorption energies in one forward pass using an equivariant graph neural network focused on the adsorbate and nearby surface atoms.
engineering_relevance: Its local representation supports efficient catalyst screening and local interface relaxation without processing the full atomic system.
method: Build a cutoff-based local graph containing adsorbate atoms and nearby surface neighbors.
Use scalar–vector message passing to encode interatomic distances and directions and predict atom-resolved energy contributions.
Obtain analytic forces by automatic differentiation for projected gradient descent relaxation with adaptive line search.
evidence_signal: Trained on AdsTraj’s 33,920 DFT structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates, AdsNet reports energy RMSE of 0.032 eV and force RMSE of 0.047 eV/Å.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish generalization beyond the reported metals and adsorbates; a local cutoff may also miss relevant longer-range interactions.
paper_title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
